title: When the Semester Sings
premise: Sebastian Nakamura transfers to Marrow Creek High, a school built over the ruins of a shuttered conservatory where, decades ago, a student named Odessa Vann was silenced — literally, by a scandal the town buried. Paired for a semester project with his sworn nemesis, Priya Raghavan, whose grandmother was the last person to hear Odessa sing, Sebastian discovers the old auditorium still holds recordings, letters, and a truth that could clear Odessa's name and indict the town's founding families — including Priya's. As their uneasy alliance deepens into found family with three other outcasts, the pair must choose between protecting their new friendship and telling a truth that will cost them the final audition, their reputations, and possibly each other. In the end they perform Odessa's recovered song at the spring concert, name her publicly, and accept that justice outside the law is slower, messier, and more human — and that the friendship survives precisely because they told the truth before the final audition.
about_author: Jonah Okafor is a former high school debate coach who grew up in a river town where every building seemed to have a basement nobody talked about. He writes young adult fiction about kids who refuse to let old towns keep old secrets.

chapters.title: The Careful Boy
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Three years after a betrayal at his old school, Sebastian arrives at Marrow Creek High with rules for staying invisible. He maps exits, avoids attention, and notices the auditorium everyone calls cursed. Emotional beat: loneliness dressed up as safety, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Ms. Ferro announces semester-long local history projects and pairs Sebastian with Priya Raghavan, his instant nemesis since day one. Their first meeting is pure friction — she thinks he's a coward, he thinks she's a bulldozer. Emotional beat: resentment with an unwanted spark of curiosity.

chapters.title: The Building Over the Building
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya drags Sebastian to the library archives to pick a topic fast, and he spots a photograph of the old Vann Conservatory — the structure Marrow Creek High was built on top of. Emotional beat: the thrill of a mystery neither will admit they want.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They draft a hostile contract: split the work, no personal questions, no friendship. Sebastian breaks his own rule within a week by noticing Priya hums a melody no one taught her. Emotional beat: the comedy and ache of two people guarding themselves.

chapters.title: Odessa Vann, 1968
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The archives yield a thin file: Odessa Vann, a Black scholarship student at the conservatory, expelled mid-semester in 1968, erased from every program. Emotional beat: indignation — the first time they're angry on the same side.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's grandmother, Amma, goes quiet when Odessa's name comes up, then plays an old cassette: a girl's voice, singing, cut off mid-phrase. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited silence and Priya's guilt at pressing it.

chapters.title: The Sealed Wing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following blueprints, they find the sealed sub-basement beneath the auditorium — the conservatory's old rehearsal hall, intact, dusty, full of sheet music. Emotional beat: awe curdling into unease; someone sealed this on purpose.

chapters.title: Third Chair
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Introduce the found family: Theo, the stage-crew ghost; Marisol, who knows every lock in town; Dev, Priya's ex-best-friend and reluctant tech genius. They swear the five of them in over gas-station fries. Emotional beat: the terrifying warmth of being included.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A hidden letter reveals Odessa was accused of stealing a scholarship endowment — an accusation made by the conservatory's benefactor, Aldous Merrick, whose family still runs the town bank. Emotional beat: history stops feeling like history.

chapters.title: Amma Breaks
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Confronted with the letter, Amma finally speaks: she was Odessa's roommate, and she stayed silent in 1968 to protect her own family's fragile place in town. Emotional beat: Priya's love and fury colliding; forgiveness not yet possible.

chapters.title: The Tape Continues
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev restores the damaged cassette and finds a second recording: Odessa describing the theft she witnessed — Merrick himself moving the money, then blaming her. Emotional beat: proof, and the vertigo of holding it.

chapters.title: Someone Knows
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The rehearsal hall has been disturbed — a chair moved, a light left on. A warning note appears in Sebastian's locker: SOME BUILDINGS STAY BURIED. Emotional beat: fear; the project is no longer academic.

chapters.title: Nemesis, Actually
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A late night in the archives turns into an accidental confession: why Sebastian left his old school (he stayed silent when a friend was scapegoated) and why Priya collects lost causes. Emotional beat: the nemesis contract quietly dies.

chapters.title: Merrick's Grandson
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The current Merrick heir, Whit, is senior class president and Sebastian's lab partner — and starts asking suspiciously friendly questions about their project topic. Emotional beat: paranoia wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Marisol's Keys
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals her own stake: her great-aunt was the conservatory custodian fired the week Odessa was expelled. The five realize the town silenced a whole constellation of people. Emotional beat: grief becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Midterm Presentation
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They present a sanitized version to Ms. Ferro, who sees through it and privately tells them: don't stop at safe. Emotional beat: an adult ally, and the first permission to be brave.

chapters.title: Whit's Offer
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Whit offers to fund their project — and quietly suggests they focus on the conservatory's architecture, not its people. Priya declines, and knows she's declared war. Emotional beat: the cost of the truth coming due in advance.

chapters.title: Vandalized
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The rehearsal hall is trashed; decades of sheet music destroyed. Only the hidden recordings, which Dev moved, survive. Emotional beat: violation and rage — and proof they're over the target.

chapters.title: The Fight
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Terrified of losing his found family the way he lost his last one, Sebastian proposes burying everything. Priya calls it exactly the silence that ruined everyone. They shatter. Emotional beat: the friendship's lowest point, both of them right.

chapters.title: Amma's Tape
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Amma records her own testimony — what she saw in 1968 and what her silence cost her — and gives it to the kids freely. Emotional beat: an elder choosing courage late, and handing it down.

chapters.title: Reconciliation, Rough Draft
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian apologizes the only honest way he can: he plays Priya the recording of his old betrayal, then says he won't repeat it. They don't hug; they just start working again. Emotional beat: repair without prettiness.

chapters.title: The Bank Basement
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Following the money trail, they find the 1968 endowment ledger in the bank's historical records — with Merrick's own initials on the missing funds. Emotional beat: the smoking gun, and the fear of what holding it means.

chapters.title: Whit Finds Out
chapters.summary: Whit's POV. Whit discovers what they have and wavers — he loved his grandfather's stories and can't unhear this version. He warns them his father already knows. Emotional beat: an enemy's heir becoming a reluctant, unreliable ally.

chapters.title: The Town That Sang
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The five interview surviving townspeople; story after story confirms the pattern of silencing. Marisol's great-aunt, ninety-one, sings a bar of Odessa's song from memory. Emotional beat: a chorus assembling itself across decades.

chapters.title: Ms. Ferro's Past
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They learn Ms. Ferro tried to expose the same story as a student twenty years ago and was crushed for it. She gives them her old research. Emotional beat: inheritance — they are not the first, and must not be the next to fail.

chapters.title: Audition Season
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The spring concert auditions arrive; the five, all musicians in hiding, must decide whether to enter — and whether to smuggle Odessa's song onto the program. Emotional beat: art as the only courtroom they'll be given.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A photo of their evidence reaches the school board. Dev is suspended on a pretext; the group scatters under pressure. Emotional beat: institutions moving to protect themselves, exactly as in 1968.

chapters.title: Dev's Choice
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Offered reinstatement in exchange for handing over the ledger, Dev refuses — his quietest, bravest moment. Emotional beat: the cost of the truth, paid by the gentlest member.

chapters.title: Sebastian's Speech
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At a school board meeting, Sebastian — the boy built for silence — stands and speaks Odessa's name into the record. Emotional beat: the careful boy's rules burning down around him, gloriously.

chapters.title: The Backlash
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The town splits; Amma's shop is boycotted; Priya's parents waver. Priya nearly recants to protect Amma, and Amma forbids it. Emotional beat: love under siege, and the older woman holding the line.

chapters.title: What Whit Does
chapters.summary: Whit's POV. Whit gives the group his grandfather's private letters — including Odessa's unanswered plea for help — then faces his father's wrath. Emotional beat: a traitor to his own house, and finally at peace with it.

chapters.title: Rehearsal in the Ruins
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The five sneak into the rehearsal hall to learn Odessa's recovered song, singing in the room where she was silenced. Emotional beat: communion with the dead girl who started everything; joy inside grief.

chapters.title: The Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The principal threatens to cancel the concert unless the project is withdrawn. The five face the choice the blurb promised: the friendship or the truth. They choose the truth — together, terrified. Emotional beat: the pact that defines them.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On the eve of the concert, with the performance uncertain and the friendship strained to snapping, Sebastian and Priya finally say out loud what the semester made them: family. Emotional beat: tenderness at maximum voltage.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At the audition, officials try to strike Odessa's song from the program. The five perform it anyway, uninvited, in the auditorium above the sealed hall — and the audience, including Amma, rises. Emotional beat: the climax; a silenced voice filling the room built over her silence.

chapters.title: The Song Goes Public
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. A phone video of the performance goes viral; the ledger reaches a journalist; the county opens an inquiry. Nothing is fixed by law yet — but the record is no longer theirs alone to hold. Emotional beat: relief that isn't victory yet.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The town holds its first public reckoning: testimony, apologies, the renaming debate. Marisol's great-aunt speaks, and the custodian's family is named at last. Emotional beat: justice outside the law — slow, partial, real.

chapters.title: Odessa's Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The school dedicates a plaque and a music scholarship to Odessa Vann; her surviving niece attends. Sebastian, who once mapped exits, stands at the front of the room. Emotional beat: the erased girl restored; the careful boy unhidden.

chapters.title: Semester's End
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Grades are posted; the project earns an A that means nothing and everything. The five make plans for summer, and Priya and Sebastian finally name what they are to each other without flinching. Emotional beat: the found family, permanent.

chapters.title: When the Semester Sings
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Closing frame: a year later, the rehearsal hall is reopened as a music room. On the first day, a new nervous kid walks in, and the five — now six — make room. Emotional beat: the song continues; memory kept alive on purpose.
